sections.overview: The catalogue name *Liomys adspersus* is the former combination for the currently accepted *Heteromys adspersus*, a spiny pocket mouse endemic to Panama.
sections.identification: Like other Panamanian pocket mice, it has fur-lined cheek pouches, somewhat stiff dorsal hairs, dark upperparts and pale underparts.
sections.habitat: Known mainly from central Panama’s Pacific slope, it occupies dry forest, thorn scrub and weedy fields and tolerates some disturbance.
sections.diet: It eats palm nuts, other seeds and plant material, as well as insects.
sections.behavior: It carries seeds in its cheek pouches and stores them in burrows or shallow pits; individuals are solitary, although wild home ranges may overlap.
sections.reproduction: Breeding is recorded from December to May in central Panama; the season may vary elsewhere.
sections.ecology: Its seed caches make it both a seed predator and a potential seed disperser when some stored seeds are not recovered. The older *Liomys* literature compares it with other spiny pocket mice, while modern classifications place it in *Heteromys*.
sections.conservation: The 2016 IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern, citing its distribution and habitat tolerance; local trends may differ.
